claims.text: The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is as-cast, homogeneous, and single-phase.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi reduces solute drag in the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
Removing Co reduces dynamic strain-aging effects in FeNiCrMn.
Co removal shifts the onset of serrated flow to lower temperatures and strain rates than in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Co removal shifts the onset of yield strengthening to lower temperatures and strain rates than in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Temperature- and strain-rate-dependent changes in dislocation density and dislocation interactions mediate the dynamic response.
The absence of Co reduces solute-dislocation locking in FeNiCrMn.
Cottrell-atmosphere interactions, solute pinning, and dynamic strain aging can produce serrations through interactions with moving dislocations.
Removing Co lowers activation barriers for dislocation motion in FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co shifts the dynamic-strain-aging regime in temperature–strain-rate space.
The Co-free alloy will show a pronounced yield-stress increase at lower temperatures or strain rates than the equiatomic baseline.
The Co-free alloy will show marked serrations at lower temperatures or strain rates than the equiatomic baseline.
When dynamic strain aging becomes operative, the Co-free alloy will have a steeper flow-stress response than the equiatomic baseline.
As-cast NiCrFeCoMn exhibits increasing yield strength sensitivity as strain rate increases and marked serrations above 900 s^-1.
The proposed comparison applies from approximately 77 K to 500 °C and from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^2 s^-1.
The proposed comparison is limited to as-cast, single-phase alloys and may not extend to differently processed or multiphase materials.
Parallel isothermal tensile tests with strain-rate jumps and identical conditions for the Co-free alloy and equiatomic baseline provide the controlled comparison.
Failure to observe either an earlier serration onset or a steeper yield-stress increase with strain rate in the Co-free alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
